answer: Ocean lantern kernel: a $58 solar buoy lantern (chandlery receipt) is the kernel of each identity, moored offshore and flashing a unique pulse code from its firmware. The harbor's tide camera records each flash against the tide table and the ocean swell — a genuine lantern rides the swell, so a recording made on shore flashes dead level and fails on the spot. A shared buoy gives itself away at once: the same pulse code twice means two aliases, and the register drops both names together. Every fake must therefore buy, moor, and tend a lantern of its own.
